name: Muttekopf
kurzbeschreibung: Towering at 2,774 metres above Imst, the prominent Muttekopf is a premier viewpoint in the Lechtal Alps, offering challenging alpine hikes, refuges, and via ferrata climbs.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Muttekopf (2,774 m) is the commanding landmark peak of Imst, forming the southeastern cornerstone of the Lechtal Alps in the Tyrolean Oberland. Owing to its isolated, forward-thrust position high above the Inn and Gurgl valleys, this handsome summit is renowned as one of the most rewarding viewpoints in the entire Tyrol region. From its spacious summit plateau, the panoramic view encompasses the Ötztaler and Stubai Alps, the Wetterstein range with Germany's Zugspitze, and extends deep into the Karwendel. Defined by striking conglomerate crags and rugged limestone cirques, the terrain around the Malchitt cirque captivates mountaineers, rock climbers, and via ferrata enthusiasts with its rich alpine flora and extraordinary geology.

Route & Anforderungen

Conquering the Muttekopf is a strenuous high-alpine endeavor involving between 800 and 1,800 metres of elevation gain depending on the chosen route. A popular, energy-saving approach utilizes the Imster Bergbahnen chairlifts via Untermarkter Alm up to the Alpjoch mountain station (2,050 m). From Alpjoch, the sensational Drischlsteig—a well-protected path carved into sheer rock—traverses across to the welcoming Muttekopfhütte (1,934 m). The route then ascends through the expansive cirque to the Muttekopfscharte gap and continues along a steep, rocky ridge to the summit cross. Sturdy boots, surefootedness, and vertigo freedom are essential. Climbers will also find top-tier challenges in the demanding Imster Klettersteig and the scenic Waterfall Via Ferrata nearby.

Besuch & Anreise

The excursion begins in Imst in the Upper Inn Valley. The base terminal of the Imster Bergbahnen in Hoch-Imst features ample parking and is easily accessed by car or by local bus from Imst-Pitztal railway station. Hikers who prefer ascending entirely on foot can hike from Imst through the romantic Rosengartenschlucht gorge to Hoch-Imst and onward to the refuge in roughly four hours. The Muttekopfhütte provides food and lodging from early June through early October.

Tipps

Resting on the sun-soaked terrace of the Muttekopfhütte is a treat in itself, famous for generous Tyrolean dumplings and vistas of the surrounding peaks. For families and thrill-seekers, pairing the mountain hike with a descent on the Alpine Coaster in Hoch-Imst—one of the world's longest alpine coasters—delivers unmatched excitement.
preis: Free access (Imst cable car optional for a fee)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; mountain tours recommended June to October
